implementationSteps: Find at most one root ui-toasts region; validate presence flag and C13 options. Otherwise create one root-owned polite live status region and visible list on first toast.
Render message with textContent, never HTML; reject object/array message values unless already formatted. Null/empty text does not enqueue.
Add unique toast owner, text, native labeled dismiss button, and 5000 ms default expiry; cap visible queue at five with FIFO cleanup.
Pause countdown on hover/focus-inside, resume remaining time on exit, and allow duration 0 for configured persistent region. Timers use owner registration.
Announce additions politely without reannouncing the whole queue; do not use an assertive global error mechanism.
On root unmount remove module-created region, preserve authored region element until normal root disposal, and clear every toast timer/listener.

implementationSteps: Validate one descendant tablist, tab elements, corresponding unique tabpanel IDs, aria-controls/labelledby relationships, and no ownership crossing into nested tabs widgets.
Validate options; choose first enabled aria-selected=true tab or first enabled tab. Reject multiple initially selected tabs with a diagnostic and use the first in DOM order deterministically.
Apply roving tabindex (focused enabled tab=0, others=-1), aria-selected on active tab, and hidden on inactive panels without removing labels.
Handle horizontal Left/Right honoring RTL; vertical Up/Down; Home/End; Enter/Space activation in manual mode. Automatic option activates with focus. Prevent default only for handled keys.
Skip disabled/aria-disabled tabs. Click activates an eligible native tab control; never convert generic markup into unnamed interactive controls.

implementationSteps: Define C13 token values on :root and use low-specificity :where selectors for native typography/buttons/controls. Keep global rules limited to documented baseline styling.

Use logical properties for margins/padding/borders, wrapping text and flexible control widths. No fixed viewport heights that hide form content at zoom.
Style valid focus outlines, disabled states, field errors and native dialogs without changing semantics. Ensure hidden stays display:none regardless of layout utility rules.

Traverse native template contents using the same declaration/structural boundaries as runtime. Identify roots, components, imports, routes, scopes, aliases, refs, and form placement statically.
Reuse expression/command parsers, prop schemas, route pattern compiler, option validator, and exact allowed/conflicting directive rules. Do not duplicate semantics in independent regexes.

Report compile-provable errors for duplicate names/aliases, unknown directives, missing modules declared in CLI manifest, bad patterns, bad literals, unsafe literal URLs, missing props, and invalid ownership combinations.
Report warnings for unresolved dynamic values, unknown runtime registrations without a manifest, API response shapes, and adapter behavior. Do not classify uncertainty as a proven runtime error.

tasks.title: Expose deterministic CLI validate and build commands
implementationSteps: Implement `plainui validate <paths...> --root <dir> --manifest <file> --format text|json --warnings-as-errors`. Defaults: root=current directory, format=text, warnings do not fail.
Implement directory recursion for `.html` and explicitly listed component files, sorted lexically. Do not read node_modules/dist/hidden directories unless explicitly passed.
Exit codes: 0=no errors, 1=validation findings, 2=usage/I/O/config failure. JSON output is one object `{schemaVersion,files,diagnostics,summary}` with no extra stdout noise.

Manifest schema: `modules` string array; `registrations` object containing command/formatter/behavior names and adapter name/version pairs; `assetRoot` project-relative directory; `assets` array of extra project-relative application files (including ESM bootstrap files). Missing fields default to empty collections and assetRoot='.'. Reject unknown manifest keys. Without a manifest, unresolved runtime registrations/modules produce warnings rather than invented certainty.

Implement `plainui build <entry.html> --out-dir <dir> --modules router,fragments,ui --minify`. Validate first; copy the entry, statically referenced local components/assets, and manifest-listed application assets preserving project-relative paths. Recognize PlainUI script/link references by exact distribution basenames from C02 and rewrite those references to `./assets/<version>/<basename>` in output. Leave other URLs unchanged; reject local asset references escaping project root. Do not transform arbitrary application JS or require compilation for normal usage.

Reject output equal to or containing source root; never recursively wipe an arbitrary output directory. Write a staging directory then atomically replace only files listed in previous build manifest, preserving unrelated files.
Provide `--help`, `--version`, and Windows path-with-spaces coverage. No create-app/scaffolding feature is required for 1.0.

tasks.title: Generate directive and API references

Publish manually explained public API pages backed by actual exported TS declarations and type tests; cover ready, diagnostics, inspector, module installation, abort behavior, readonly values, and App vs lexical resolution.
Document all stable diagnostic codes with safe example, cause, effect on current output, and concrete remedy. Explain errors versus warnings.
Document exact grammar/precedence/truthiness/limits, URL encoding, writable paths, formatter input/output, and command/lifecycle ordering.

tasks.title: Finalize package exports and zero-build assets
implementationSteps: Export plainui root ESM/types, router/fragments/ui ESM installers, stylesheet, and schema. Keep internal workspace modules private and inaccessible through documented exports.
Emit all C02 classic/ESM filenames from the same versioned source. Use sourceMappingURL references pointing to shipped maps, and include notices for bundled dependencies.

Pack into local tarballs and install into a new temporary consumer project. Test package ESM imports, plain JS usage, type resolution, CLI executable, and local classic files.
Run zero-build HTML from a plain HTTP server with no node_modules/bundler/CDN access and verify optional modules loaded after core before DOM-ready boot.
Verify ESM import alone never mounts roots and loading classic+ESM on an already active root fails exactly once without double listeners.

tasks.title: Implement development diagnostics inspection
implementationSteps: Complete inspector snapshot fields: root lifecycle, owner counts by kind, live binding/subscriber/timer/listener counts, pending action count, cache entry count, and redacted resource record metadata.

Resource inspection exposes generated ID, status, loading/refreshing/stale flags, updatedAt, and error kind/code/status only. Exclude raw data, URLs with queries, headers, body, messages from backend, and persisted values.
Snapshot returns frozen detached data; inspection does not subscribe, trigger fetch, retain DOM, or invoke formatters.
Provide a minimal developer example that renders this data as text using public APIs. Do not build an IDE, browser extension, or telemetry service.
Verify production debug=false rejects inspection while ordinary diagnostics remain available with safe code/location.
Test counters under shared transports and destination-linked fragment ranges so shared objects are counted once and consumers separately.

tasks.title: Define independent backend and sample-data contracts
implementationSteps: Use the exact endpoint/data shapes in 08-test-vectors. Freeze them as JSON Schema-like fixture contracts without imposing these application envelopes on framework users.

Define deterministic seed IDs/prices/content, pagination/query filters, successful/empty responses, validation envelopes, delay/error switches available only to test servers, and request correlation IDs.
Define server-authoritative cart/checkout recomputation from product database values; ignore client-supplied prices/totals. Expose an order lookup endpoint for uncertain mutation reconciliation.
Provide identity-envelope and alternate-envelope response modes via the two backend implementations and register one explicit adapter for the alternate shape.
Keep frontend component sources byte-identical between backend runs; only app-level adapter/baseURL bootstrap configuration may change. Record component file hashes in compatibility tests.
Specify cookie-authenticated demo session endpoints and CSRF meta token injection; label demo credentials/data as sample-only and avoid production authentication claims.
tasks.acceptance: contract fixture validator accepts all seeded successes/errors and rejects malformed shapes; example requirements map to endpoints with no undefined backend behavior.

Implement multipart uploads with busboy 1.6.0 on Node and python-multipart 0.0.32 on Python. Use busboy field/file callbacks and Python parse_form callbacks to collect the ordered field/file metadata defined in 08-test-vectors. Enforce a 2 MiB total request limit, 1 MiB per file, four files, twenty fields, and 1 KiB field values before retaining data; reject limit violations with HTTP 413. See the [busboy API](https://github.com/mscdex/busboy) and [python-multipart API](https://multipart.fastapiexpert.com/api/). Never interpret uploaded filenames as disk paths; store bytes only in temporary test-owned storage.
Implement explicit test-only delay/error barriers, deterministic reset endpoint bound to loopback/test mode, and cookie/CSRF/session reset behavior.
Add startup flags host/port/data-dir, graceful shutdown, isolated temp storage, and no outbound services. Document one command per server and fixed test ports with collision detection.

Enhance search using query state/resources with loading/error/empty/result views, manual retry, encoded query handling, and safe text rendering.
Add client article routes, required fallback, title expressions, and focus/scroll handling while documenting server metadata/HTTP status limitations.

Build edit form with mapped literal-name server errors, unsaved-change guard, pending/retry displays, and explicit reset. Preserve values on all failures.
Add dialog confirmation, manual tabs, and chart behavior using public APIs plus inner ui-ignore. Keep labels and headings meaningful.

Provide complete blog/storefront/SaaS walkthroughs and Node/Python backend recipes with exact commands, request/response bodies, error adapters, and server route fallback configuration.

Audit public extension APIs for postdisposal writes and ownership crossing; review all HTML/URL/attribute sinks and package dependencies using actual advisory data at qualification time.

tasks.title: Run automated accessibility and keyboard tests

Script keyboard-only main workflows with Tab/Shift+Tab/arrows/Home/End/Enter/Space/Escape and assert focus order/visibility.

tasks.acceptance: signed actual manual report covers all three apps and required UI helpers, with no unresolved blocking accessibility issue.

tasks.title: Qualify actual release browsers
implementationSteps: At RC preparation, consult official vendor releases and record current and immediately previous stable desktop Chromium/Chrome, Firefox, and Safari; current iOS Safari and Android Chrome. Record exact version/build/OS/device and date.
Keep Playwright engine CI as fast regression coverage, but run qualification on the actual release browsers; patched Playwright Firefox/WebKit are not proof of branded Firefox/Safari support.
Use WebDriver/safaridriver or a pinned external browser lab for unsupported local combinations; record provider/session evidence. Real iOS/Android devices are required for mobile qualification.
Execute the complete high-risk browser scenarios: native forms/files/IME, history traversal correction, focus/scroll, dialogs, import parsing, fragment sanitizer, persistence, and module startup.

tasks.acceptance: every required actual-browser cell has an evidence link and passes; version numbers are collected at release, not guessed from the planning date.

tasks.title: Measure bundle size and performance budgets
implementationSteps: Select and reserve one physical reference machine before beta; record CPU/model/core count/RAM/OS/kernel/browser build, display, power mode, plugged-in state, background workload policy, tool versions, and commit. Do not report invented hardware values.

Measure production files with deterministic gzip level 9, mtime=0. Core budget is <=35840 bytes; sum core+router+fragments+UI compressed file sizes is <=71680 bytes, including sanitizer and runtime dependencies. Report ESM/classic independently and gate on the larger delivered variant.

Benchmark 1000 keyed list items with actual visible rows and ten existing items changed per update, keeping key/order stable. Force scheduler flush completion as timing endpoint; include JS plus DOM commit, report layout/paint separately from a browser trace.

Run 30 warmups, then 200 measured updates per run, at least five runs after page reload. Use nearest-rank percentile (sorted sample index ceil(.95*n)-1); each run's p95 must be <16ms. Report p50/p95 and raw samples, not best run only.

Also measure ten-key reorders as a diagnostic and cold boot of 1000 bindings, component import waterfalls, and 100 route transitions. Do not silently replace the fixed hard-gate fixture with an easier operation.
If gates fail, profile and fix without removing required functionality/security; otherwise revise RFC budget transparently and retain old/new measurements.
tasks.acceptance: reproducible scripts, exact manifest, raw traces/samples, module sizes, and pass/fail calculations published before beta. Goals are not marked achieved until measured.

tasks.title: Measure lifetime reliability and memory plateau
implementationSteps: Instrument owners/listeners/timers/observers/request subscribers/cache entries and run 100 route transitions with components, slots, forms, fragments, widgets, and active requests.
After each route disposal require route-local counts return to shared-shell baseline. After root unmount require all framework counts zero and cache<=maxEntries throughout.
Collect forced-GC heap samples using a documented browser test protocol every ten transitions after twenty warmups; never expose GC as application API.

Define plateau tolerance before measuring: final five post-GC samples may not show >5% or >1MiB growth (whichever is larger) over first five steady-state samples, and retained framework owner/node counts must not grow. This is a plan-selected diagnostic threshold to record in benchmark manifest, not a supplied measured result.
Distinguish library/application-retained nodes from framework retention via retainer paths. Fix framework leaks even if aggregate heap remains within tolerance.
Repeat full mount/unmount 100 times and test failure teardown (import timeout, sanitizer error, throwing behavior cleanup, interrupted guards) to catch error-path leaks.
tasks.acceptance: zero lifecycle counters after unmount, bounded cache, stable retained ownership, documented heap plateau, and no untriaged framework retention.

tasks.title: Close full conformance and beta gate
implementationSteps: Reconcile every RFC/design clause and C01–C14 decision against 07-coverage and executable fixture IDs. Every directive family requires valid, invalid, lifecycle, and alias cases.

Run all suites against minified classic and ESM production artifacts, not just source modules. Include parser property tests, seeded races, CLI parity, strict CSP, actual-browser matrix, and example compatibility.
Verify all release evidence references the same candidate commit and locked dependencies; stale reports are not accepted without a documented unaffected-scope justification.
Require contract clarifications accepted, no unresolved critical bugs, all required docs/examples delivered, measured budgets passed, and manual security/accessibility evidence present.
Build check-release to output a per-gate pass/fail/pending report and exit nonzero for either fail or pending. Do not implement force/ignore-required-gate switches.
Publish beta artifacts only after the beta readiness report is complete; optional modules remain mandatory release deliverables.
tasks.acceptance: all traceability entries resolved, check-release passes with real evidence, and M6 explicitly distinguishes completed facts from prospective RC steps.

tasks.title: Prepare release candidate and compatibility record
implementationSteps: Assign a single `1.0.0-rc.1` version across public runtime/CLI/assets/module bridge metadata; rebuild and pack from a clean checkout using frozen lockfile.
Produce changelog describing complete scope, known nonblocking limitations, security properties, supported browsers, and performance reference hardware/results without universal claims.
Record accepted spec revision, task/requirement evidence hashes, dependency/license inventory, and exact artifact integrity hashes.
Install RC tarballs into fresh zero-build and module consumers and run full example smoke tests, strict CSP, and key browser checks.
Freeze behavioral changes after RC; any fix changes version to next RC and reruns affected verification plus release manifest integrity.
Document post-1.0 semver rules and vulnerability-reporting contact supplied by maintainer. Do not invent a contact address.
tasks.acceptance: reproducible RC artifact set with all matching evidence and explicit limitation notes; no unresolved publishing identity/contact questions hidden in code.

tasks.title: Verify publishing identity licenses and reproducibility
implementationSteps: Verify actual ownership/availability of planned package names and remote repository. Use maintainer-supplied publisher identity; do not register accounts or reserve names implicitly.
Use MIT as the proposed project license, subject to rights-holder confirmation, and preserve dependency license notices. Do not falsely assert copyright ownership on the user's behalf.
Configure CI release credentials through secret storage with least necessary publish scope; never commit tokens or expose them in artifact metadata.
Rebuild twice in clean isolated directories and compare all artifact hashes, excluding explicitly normalized provenance timestamps. Fix nondeterministic output before release.
Run dry-run pack/publish validation, file allowlist checks, source map integrity, exports install tests, and unwanted-file/secret scan.

Prepare a concrete release report listing package names/versions, files, hashes, license/identity confirmation, tag, and public destination before any publishing authorization step in the future implementation workflow.
tasks.acceptance: publishing prerequisites are facts, not guesses; dry run passes; reproducibility verified; unavailable legal/account ownership remains an explicit external release blocker.

tasks.title: Publish the complete 1.0 release
implementationSteps: Re-run check-release on final 1.0.0 candidate and confirm accepted public contract, identity, and artifact report. This planning task does not itself authorize publishing future artifacts.
When the maintainer authorizes the concrete release, tag the exact tested commit and publish the already verified runtime/CLI packages and versioned static assets through the release job.
Upload docs, schema, licenses, integrity manifest, browser matrix, benchmark manifests/traces, and source maps with matching version identifiers.
Install from published package endpoints in a clean consumer and fetch versioned static files; compare integrity with prepared manifest and run smoke tests.
If postpublication verification fails, stop promotion and issue an explicit corrective patch/notice. Do not silently overwrite immutable published versions or claim complete success.
Record artifact URLs, registry versions, tag/commit, verification outcome, and publication timestamp from actual results.
tasks.acceptance: all required artifacts published and verified, no module omitted, final evidence references the shipped bytes, and release announcement claims only proven gates.

tasks.title: Establish maintenance and regression policy
implementationSteps: Require schema/fixtures/docs updates for every directive/API/default/lifecycle change. Existing behavior changes are major unless correcting a documented security defect.
Define dependency update process: exact pin, lockfile, security corpus, browser conformance, size report, and migration note when needed.
Preserve regression fixtures for every production bug, minimized property-test failure, and sanitizer advisory fix.
Document how to rerun benchmarks on the recorded machine and update browser support evidence for later releases without retroactively changing 1.0 claims.
Create a post-1.0 backlog containing excluded features only as future proposals; do not describe them as supported 1.0 features.
Document security-report handling and patch publication with clear migration guidance; use confirmed project contacts only.
tasks.acceptance: contributors can reproduce validation and release checks, policy matches semantic versioning rules, and 1.0 artifacts/evidence remain immutable and traceable.
